scenes.say: Merge or rebase? Which one should you use when working with Git branches?
Merging combines branches and keeps the full history, adding a merge commit. Rebasing moves your commits onto another branch, rewriting history for a straight line.

scenes.title: How it looks in Git
scenes.say: With git merge main, you get a merge commit. With git rebase main, your commits are replayed onto main for a cleaner history.

scenes.label: When?
scenes.sub: Rebase for local branches, merge for shared ones.
scenes.say: I use rebase for my own local branches to keep things tidy, and merge when combining shared branches to preserve the full history.

scenes.question: Should you rebase a shared branch?
scenes.wrong: Yes, always rebase for clean history.
scenes.right: No—rebasing shared branches rewrites history for others.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Should you rebase a shared branch? No—rebasing shared branches rewrites history and can mess up your teammates.
